factual_and_methodological.summary: IMF primary evidence confirms 191 members, current quotas of SDR476bn, roughly US$1tn of nonconcessional lending firepower, the approved but not yet effective SDR715.7bn post-16th-review quota total, and the September 23, 2026 formal voting shares used in the dossier. The report treats conditionality as a financing mechanism under member governance rather than unlimited political control.

editorial_publication_readiness.opening: Direct mechanism-led opening; no generic sophistication claims or product-process narration.
editorial_publication_readiness.headings: Headings advance the actor-specific mechanism, constraints, contrary evidence and revision conditions.
editorial_publication_readiness.language_localization: EN and PT-BR are semantically aligned; PT-BR technical prose was localized before approval.
editorial_publication_readiness.cohesion: Argument moves from rights/capability through transmission, constraints and evidence that would revise the assessment.
editorial_publication_readiness.template_meta_qa: No prompt, QA-process, schema, renderer or roadmap leakage detected.

contextual_depth.summary: The dossier distinguishes legal rights, operating capability, transmission, substitutability and institutional constraints rather than relying on scale or reputation.

visual_evidence_readiness.signature: At least two analytical tables, one quantitative chart, one causal flow and one mind map in both locales.
visual_evidence_readiness.limitations: Visuals encode sourced quantities or mechanisms defended in prose and are not combined into a synthetic power score.

contrary_evidence: Alternative bilateral, regional or market financing can reduce the Fund's leverage in a given episode.
Programme approval and review do not guarantee creditor coordination, market access or policy success.
limitations: Catalytic effects on other financing are episode-specific and harder to establish than the formal lending and governance channels.
Quota reform should remain described as approved but not effective until the implementation conditions are actually met.
notes: Dedicated single-actor Strategic Actors dossier. Primary-source factual core, controlled taxonomy, bilingual parity and visual evidence reviewed; no public bundle for this ID at approval time.

en.title: IMF: pooled sovereign resources, conditional finance and the architecture of balance-of-payments support
en.deck: The IMF pools resources from 191 members and combines crisis lending with programme frameworks, surveillance and multilateral governance. Its structural role changes financing constraints; national authorities retain responsibility for implementation.
en.regime: The IMF is shifting toward a larger quota-based permanent resource base while retaining supplementary borrowing and conditional programme lending.
en.key_risk: Programme conditionality can be overstated as direct political control, while approved quota reform can be misreported as already-effective resources.

pt-BR.title: FMI: recursos soberanos compartilhados, financiamento condicional e a arquitetura de apoio ao balanço de pagamentos
pt-BR.deck: O FMI reúne recursos de 191 membros e combina crédito de crise com programas, supervisão e governança multilateral. Seu papel altera restrições financeiras; autoridades nacionais continuam responsáveis pela implementação.
pt-BR.regime: O FMI caminha para uma base permanente maior de quotas, mantendo recursos emprestados suplementares e crédito condicionado a programas.
pt-BR.key_risk: Condicionalidade pode ser exagerada como controle político direto, e uma reforma aprovada pode ser descrita incorretamente como recurso já vigente.

publication.selection_rationale: The IMF is an active Strategic Actors record with documented global-financing and sovereign-financing-framework channels but lacked a dedicated single-actor canonical study.
